items.title: Sonny Rollins — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Raglan coat, you know, like the kind Basil Rathbone wrote in Sherlock Holmes, that type of coat.

ctx.x: So, if you work a smaller club, or you didn’t get paid, what could you do?

Well, um...as I said when you say “smaller club,” I worked many places where I didn’t get paid. I’ve worked places where my overcoat was stolen. I’ve worked places where uh...oh boy, I hate to, I’ve got a mental block so I don’t have to relive those days, but I worked plenty of those places where I didn’t get paid, for one reason or another. I mean, we just expected that as musicians, you know. Uh...I, I say that because well there’s a place in Brooklyn that might have been a mob-owned, Tony–I don’t know, it was…

Hmm. We’ve talked earlier about how you learned to improvise...and you use instinct, basically, and I wonder: how did you learn to “swing?” Or did you have to learn? Did you, were you always swinging?
